description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING.

`UNIVERSAL::DOES` has its OWN guard in perl, different from
`UNIVERSAL::isa`'s: XS_UNIVERSAL_DOES croaks on an unblessed invocant where
isa quietly answers '':

    perl -e 'eval { UNIVERSAL::DOES([], "foo") }; print $@'
    Can't call method "DOES" on unblessed reference at -e line 1.

    perl -e 'no warnings; printf "[%s]\n", UNIVERSAL::isa([], "foo")'
    []

PCL's `UNIVERSAL::pl-DOES` is `(pl-isa obj class)` -- one line, no guard -- so
the call RUNS and answers ''.

THIS IS A LIVE BASELINE ROW: t/uni/universal.t test 85, "DOES call error
message says DOES, not isa", `like($@, qr/Can't call method "DOES" on
unblessed reference/)`.  It is the ONE row of that file this round does not
attribute to #1736/#1737, and its cause is this.  (The METHOD spelling
`$unblessed_ref->DOES(...)` already dies correctly -- probed -- so only the
FUNCTION spelling is missing the check.)

FIX: in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's UNIVERSAL package, `pl-DOES` checks that the
invocant is a BLESSED reference (p-get-class / the blessed predicate the
method dispatch uses) and otherwise dies perl-shaped, naming DOES.  Note the
method arms (`(string-equal method-name "DOES") (apply #'p-isa ...)`) must be
left alone: they are reached only after the dispatch has already resolved a
class, so they cannot see this case and must not grow a second copy of the
check (rule 11).
subject: UNIVERSAL::DOES on an unblessed ref dies in perl and RUNS in PCL -- pl-DOES has no guard of its own; t/uni/universal.t test 85
